claim:
WHO SWITCHES WHOM, K562 (causal). Effect z of a target = its change / the sd of that gene across the screen's
        non-targeting controls. Regulators: knockdowns with a phenotype (energy test p < 0.05). FOUND in the genome-wide
        screen: |z| >= 4, top 300 per regulator, the regulator itself and genes whose TSS is within 50 kb of its TSS
        excluded (CRISPRi can silence neighbours). CONFIRMED in the essential screen (independent experiment, same
        regulator and target): the target's effect standardised within that knockdown's own row (median / MAD: its
        effect beyond the knockdown's overall shift), same sign, BH q < 0.05 over everything testable. (Set after the
        trial: confirming on control-scaled z let a strong knockdown's random targets pass; shuffled targets confirmed
        16% as many links as real ones.) Knockdown lowers the target ->
        ACTIV

DO K562 ACTIVATIONS SHOW ACROSS THE BODY'S CELL TYPES? Correlation across CELLxGENE cell types (log profiles) of
        regulator and target, confirmed activator edges vs random pairs with the same regulators and targets matched
        on expression level: AUROC >= 0.55 and permutation p < 0.05 (200 draws).

A SWITCH MAP FOR ALL CELL TYPES. Transcription factor -> gene co-expression across cell types, tissues split
        in two halves (sha256): FOUND r >= 0.5 in one half's cell-type profiles (top 100 per TF), CONFIRMED r >= 0.4
        in the other half's. CLAIM: these co-expression links predict causal activation in K562 (knockdown lowers the
        gene, z <= -4, cis excluded) better than other TF-gene pairs testable there: Fisher OR >= 1.5, p < 0.05.
        Negative: TF labels shuffled (OR within 0.67-1.5).

text: Disclosed before testing. Trial runs (300 regulators, 150 TFs; part A on all data) were looked at: R1 with control-scaled confirmation let shuffled targets confirm 368 vs 2,347 real, so confirmation was changed to a within-knockdown standardised effect (shuffled then 31 vs 1,598); R1 known answers untestable in the trial subset. R2 on the trial edges: AUROC 0.437 (activations less co-expressed across cell types than level-matched random pairs; median r 0.095 vs 0.195); R2 not changed. R3 on 150 TFs: 11,447 links, 35 K562 truth positives, OR 0; shuffled-gene confirmation 17% of real; R3 not changed. These regulators and TFs are part of the full test, so R2 and R3 are not blind for them.

Disclosed before testing. Trial runs on subsets (700 essential knockdowns, 300 TFs, 400 genome-wide knockdowns) printed ONLY the controls and sizes; no real outcome of G2-X1, X2, L1 or L2 was computed for display or seen. Seen: X1 eligible 68 of 769 knockdowns; X1 negative (noise only) gaps 0.006/-0.003/-0.001, not passed; planted gaps 0.56, passed. X2 negative mean Spearman -0.011, planted 0.447. L1 negative median gain 0.0 (exact zeros where the two random knockdowns coincide, ~1/770 of links; symmetric), planted 0.195. L2 first trial: one mediator shuffle gave odds ratio 1.87 (p 0.30) with only 81 curated links, outside the 0.67-1.5 window; a controls-only check over 3 shuffles showed it swings 0.7-1.9 by chance (z-decile strata) and is near 1 with |z| x |lfc| strata. Changed before declaring (commit 'generegx G2-L2 (after the trial...)'): strata |z| quintiles x |lfc| quintiles; 20 shuffles, geometric-mean OR as the negative, all 20 as an empirical null for the real OR. Re-trial: negative geometric mean 0.99, planted 100%. Data check before the claims were written: K562 genome-wide p column inconsistent with lfc/lfcSE, so Wald p from lfc/lfcSE is used for all five screens.

claim:
INFLUENCE CHANGES WITH CELL TYPE, BEYOND EXPERIMENT NOISE. Knockdowns in all five screens; targets measured
        in all five. Per knockdown, agreement of two screens = Pearson r of its target log2 fold changes, corrected for
        noise: rho = r / sqrt(rel_A x rel_B), rel = 1 - mean(lfcSE^2) / var(lfc) over the same targets. Knockdowns
        with rel >= 0.2 in all five screens. Reference: rho(K562 essential, K562 genome-wide), same cell type, two
        experiments. CLAIM, for each of RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat: gap = rho_ref - rho(K562 essential, that cell type) is
        positive (one-sided sign test over knockdowns p < 0.05) with median gap >= 0.05. Negative (must not pass): the
        other cell type replaced by K562 genome-wide plus noise drawn from that cell type's lfcSE. Planted (must
        pass): the same, with half of each knockdown's target effects shuffled.

A GENE INFLUENCES MORE WHERE IT IS MORE EXPRESSED. Reach of a knockdown in a cell type = share of measured
        genes it changes (links); expression = HPA cell-line RNA (K-562, hTERT-RPE1, Hep-G2, mean of the two Jurkat
        lines; log1p nTPM). Both as percentiles among the knockdowns common to the four essential screens, within each
        cell type. Knockdowns whose expression varies (range of log1p nTPM >= 1). CLAIM: mean over knockdowns of the
        Spearman correlation across the four cell types between expression and reach >= 0.10, permutation p < 0.05
        (expression's cell-type labels permuted within each knockdown, 2,000 draws). Negative (must not pass): each
        knockdown given another knockdown's expression. Planted (must pass): reach := expression + noise (sd 0.2).

AT WHAT LEVEL -- DOSE. Links significant with the same sign in >= 2 of the four cell types where the
        knockdown's own knockdown is usable. Per link, across those cell types: d_dose = SD of log2(|effect| /
        |own knockdown|); d_rand = the same with the own knockdown of one random other knockdown usable in those cell
        types (keeps each cell type's overall knockdown strength). CLAIM (BETTER rule): gain = d_rand - d_dose, sign
        test p < 0.05 and median gain >= +0.01 (up to 300,000 links drawn at random, seeded), i.e. a deeper knockdown
        of the same gene gives a bigger effect, so "effect per unit of knockdown" is the transferable level.
        Negative (must not pass): both arms random knockdowns. Planted (must pass): effect := own knockdown x the
        link's mean ratio x noise (sd 0.3 log2).

DIRECT OR THROUGH ANOTHER GENE (K562 genome-wide). For a transcription factor r (HPA) with CollecTRI targets
        measured, each link r -> t is INDIRECT if some mediator m explains it: m knocked down in the screen (own
        knockdown usable), r -> m and m -> t both links, and the predicted effect lfc(m | r) x lfc(t | m) / own(m) has
        the same sign as lfc(t | r) and >= half its size; otherwise DIRECT. CLAIM: direct links are more often curated
        TF -> target interactions (CollecTRI) than indirect ones: Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio over 25 strata (quintiles of
        |lfc/lfcSE| x quintiles of |lfc|, so link strength cannot drive it) >= 1.5, CMH p < 0.05, and above all 20
        shuffled-mediator odds ratios (empirical p < 0.05). Negative: mediators' effects on targets shuffled between
        mediators, 20 times; their geometric-mean odds ratio must stay within 0.67-1.5. Planted (>= 90%): 200 links set
        to a mediator's predicted effect are called indirect. (Changed after the trial, before declaring: one shuffle and
        |z| deciles alone; the trial's 81 curated links made one shuffle's odds ratio swing 0.7-1.9.)

text: Recorded after the G2 run (not part of any verdict). L2: 760 of 5,283 indirect calls name a middle gene within 1 Mb of the target; GENCODE 46 gene-level TSS for HBG2 (ENSG00000196565) is chr11:5,505,605 (readthrough-extended; the gene's real TSS is ~5.25 Mb), so HBG1/HBD escaped the 50 kb cis exclusion against HBG2 (791 calls via haemoglobin genes). Post hoc with nearby-mediator calls set aside: MH OR 1.31, CMH p 0.17 (19,360 links) -- verdict FAIL unchanged. The same TSS layer was used in G1 cis exclusion. X1 rho for the two K562 experiments is 1.12 (> 1): the noise correction slightly overshoots, i.e. the two K562 experiments agree as well as their noise allows.

claim:
X1 null: per knockdown, which of the two screens (second K562 experiment, other cell type) counts as "same
        cell type" is a coin flip (its gap changes sign); 10,000 draws per cell type. STABLE PASS if p_MC < 0.05 for
        RPE1, HepG2 and Jurkat and the full X1 gate passes in >= 95% of the 200 runs.

X2 null: expression's cell-type labels permuted within each knockdown, 10,000 draws. STABLE FAIL if
        p_MC >= 0.05 and the X2 gate fails in >= 95% of the runs.

L1 null: each link's own-knockdown dose replaced by a random other gene's (usable in the same cell types),
        200 draws over all links; real = the same statistic with the true dose, its random-dose arm redrawn 200 times
        (median taken). STABLE PASS if p_MC < 0.05 and the L1 gate passes in >= 95% of the runs.

L2 null: mediators' effects on targets shuffled between mediators, 1,000 draws (MH odds ratio each).
        STABLE FAIL if p_MC >= 0.05 and the L2 gate fails in >= 95% of the runs (each run's 20-shuffle control and
        empirical null drawn from the 1,000).

text: Disclosed before the EXAM run. Model development on DEV only (fit on DEV-A knockdowns, scored on DEV-B; EXAM knockdowns never scored). Variants tried: T1 v0 raw source profiles (gain over generic K562 +0.042, RPE1 +0.004, HepG2 +0.018, Jurkat +0.033), v1 strength + specific-pattern split (K562 +0.057, RPE1 +0.009, HepG2 +0.025, Jurkat +0.044), v2 strength only (0 by construction: r is scale-free); T2 v0 (RPE1 +0.002, HepG2 +0.004, Jurkat +0.014) and v1 (RPE1 +0.003, HepG2 +0.005, Jurkat +0.016); C1 v0 raw next step (-0.002), v1 go-between patterns minus generic (+0.001), v2 strength only (0), v3 strength + specific next step (+0.0004), v4 v3 through the 50 strongest go-betweens (+0.0001), v3 shuffled (-0.0005). Chosen: v1 for T1/T2, v3 for C1 (adopted in commit 'generegp G3 (after DEV, before EXAM)'). Claim thresholds NOT changed after DEV: on DEV, T1 misses only RPE1 (gain 0.009 < 0.01), T2 passes only Jurkat, C1 fails; so T1, T2 and C1 are expected to FAIL as declared, with per-cell-type results reported. K562 two-experiment ceiling (raw r, DEV-B) 0.23 vs the K562 transfer model 0.26.

claim:
CELL DATA FROM THE OTHER CELL TYPES. For each cell type in turn held out, its profile for a knockdown =
        u x generic + v x (the knockdown's mean strength in the other three) x generic + sum of w_c x its specific
        pattern in each of the other three cell types (least squares, fit on DEV). CLAIM: BETTER than generic in all four cell types. Negative (must not be BETTER in any): the
        other cell types' profiles taken from a different knockdown (labels deranged), refit. Planted (must be BETTER
        in all): the held-out profile replaced by the mean of the other three plus noise of its own lfcSE.

CELL DATA FROM K562 ALONE (the genome-wide screen; how to predict knockdowns never screened elsewhere). For
        RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat: profile = u x generic + v x strength x generic + w x specific pattern, all from the
        knockdown's K562 genome-wide profile, fit on DEV.
        CLAIM: BETTER than generic in all three. Same negative and planted controls (single source).
        Only where this passes: predictions for every K562 genome-wide knockdown with >= 20 links that the other
        cell type never screened are written to the bank as predictions (top 30 genes, with the EXAM accuracy).

THE NEXT STEP (K562 genome-wide). Genes split by sha256('generegp-io:' + Ensembl) parity into INPUT genes
        (also knocked down in the screen, own knockdown <= -0.5) and OUTPUT genes. For knockdown A, its next step on
        the output genes = sum over input genes m that A changes (links) of [lfc(m | A) / own(m)] x lfc(outputs | m),
        i.e. what A does to m, times what m does (m's specific pattern on the outputs, its generic part removed).
        Model = u x generic + v x A's strength (from its effects on the input genes) x generic + w x next step, fit on
        DEV; scored on knockdowns
        with >= 20 output links and >= 5 input links. CLAIM: BETTER than generic AND BETTER than the same model with
        the input genes' profiles shuffled between input genes (which gene is the go-between matters). Negative
        (must not be BETTER than generic): that shuffled model. Planted (must be BETTER than generic): outputs
        replaced by the next-step prediction (scaled) plus noise of their lfcSE.

text: G4 trial on subsets (600 essential + 600 genome-wide knockdowns, small Monte Carlo counts) printed only whether controls behaved (all five: controls ok) and timings; no real outcome was shown. Design inputs looked at before writing the claims (counts only): 48,796 interacting pairs (HPA, OpenCell, Complex Portal); 14,654 with both genes in all four essential screens; per cell type ~9,200 ON, ~3,500 OFF-ROOM, 53-152 OFF-MADE; K562 genome-wide 23,413 ON, 10,943 OFF-ROOM, 560 OFF-MADE. Timing is not in the data.

claim:
SAME ROOM MATTERS. Among interacting pairs with clear effects in X: median r(ON) - median r(OFF-ROOM) >= 0.02
        and Monte Carlo p < 0.05 (ON/OFF labels permuted 10,000 times within strength quintiles), in each of the four
        essential cell types (K562 genome-wide reported).

THE INTERACTION CARRIES OVER FROM ANOTHER CELL TYPE. OpenCell pairs (measured in HEK293T) that are ON in X vs
        random non-interacting pairs that are also made and share a room (each pair's partner swapped for a random gene
        in a room it shares, same strength quintile, not cis), 1,000 Monte Carlo draws: median r gain >= 0.02 and
        p_MC < 0.05, in each of the four essential cell types.

NOT MADE -> NO PARTNERSHIP. Pooled over the five screens (all knockdowns): median r(ON) - median r(OFF-MADE)
        >= 0.02, Monte Carlo p < 0.05 (labels permuted 10,000 times within screen).

THE RULE HELPS PREDICT (on top of G3). A knockdown's profile in X predicted by the G3-T1 model (other cell
        types, strength + patterns) plus its ON partners' mean pattern measured in X (partners with clear effects;
        never its own data in X). Fit on DEV knockdowns, scored once on EXAM knockdowns with a clear effect and >= 1
        ON partner. CLAIM in each of the four cell types: BETTER than the G3-T1 model (house rule) AND Monte Carlo
        p < 0.05 against 200 draws where the partners are swapped for random genes made in X, sharing a room, with
        clear effects (same number).

PREDICT A GENE NEVER MEASURED ANYWHERE, FROM ITS PARTNERS ALONE. Model = generic + ON partners' mean pattern
        in X. Same split, scoring and Monte Carlo; BETTER than generic and p_MC < 0.05 in each of the four.

text: G5 trial on subsets (200 DepMap genes; 600 essential + 800 genome-wide knockdowns; small Monte Carlo counts) printed only whether controls behaved (all four ok) and timings; no real outcome shown. Design inputs looked at before writing the claims (counts only): 141,164 human paralog pairs, 10,815 genes with a closest paralog >= 30% identity; 1,103 DepMap lines with gene effect and RNA; 973 genes needed in >= 5% of lines with a measured substitute; 562 essential knockdowns with a substitute, 232 whose substitute's RNA varies across the four lines; knockdowns with the substitute measured: K562 298, RPE1 367, HepG2 403, Jurkat 408, K562 genome-wide 2,427.

claim:
COVER ACROSS ~1,100 CANCER CELL LINES. Genes A needed in >= 5% of lines (effect < -0.5) whose substitute is
        measured: Spearman across lines between B's RNA and A's effect (positive = more substitute, A less needed).
        CLAIM: median rho >= 0.05 and Monte Carlo p < 0.05 against 1,000 draws with matched random genes in B's place.

COVER ACROSS THE FOUR SCREENED CELL TYPES. Knockdowns in all four essential screens whose substitute's RNA
        varies (HPA range of log1p nTPM >= 1): within-knockdown Spearman across K562, RPE1, HepG2, Jurkat between B's
        RNA percentile and A's knockdown reach percentile (share of genes it changes). CLAIM: mean <= -0.10,
        permutation p < 0.05 (10,000; B's cell-type labels permuted within knockdown) and Monte Carlo p < 0.05
        against 1,000 draws with random genes whose RNA also varies in B's place.

STEPPING UP. Knocking down A (own knockdown measured, <= -0.5) raises B's mRNA. Pooled over the five screens:
        median log2 fold change of B in A's knockdown minus the mean of 1,000 Monte Carlo medians with matched random
        genes (same screen, not within 100 kb of A) >= +0.02 and p_MC < 0.05.

PREDICT WHICH CELL LINES NEED A GENE. Cell lines split DEV / EXAM by sha256('cellbrain-c1:' + ModelID) parity.
        Per gene A (G5-S1 set): least squares on DEV lines, effect ~ 1 + A's own RNA (baseline) vs + B's RNA (model);
        score = Pearson r of predicted vs measured effect on EXAM lines. CLAIM: BETTER (house rule: sign test over
        genes p < 0.05, median gain >= +0.01) AND Monte Carlo p < 0.05 against 200 draws with matched random genes in
        B's place (median gain each).
